verdicts.quote: “For apps or integrations that other people use, use the OAuth flow… Authentication: OAuth 2.0.”
verdicts.reason: ClickUp’s docs state both personal tokens and OAuth are supported, and explicitly direct third‑party apps to use OAuth2.

verdicts.quote: “The ClickUp API is available on all ClickUp plans… Anyone with a ClickUp account can generate a personal token.”
verdicts.reason: Credentials are self‑serve on the free plan (personal token), and developers can create OAuth apps from Workspace settings without partner/sales review (owners/admins).

verdicts.quote: “API Docs: ClickUp API v2 Reference… Attachments — Create Task Attachment; Comments — Get Task Comments; Create Task Comment; Get Chat View Comments.”
verdicts.reason: The reference lists many resource areas (attachments, comments, custom fields, folders, goals, lists, spaces, tags, tasks, time tracking, webhooks, views, docs v3), indicating broad coverage across the product.

verdicts.quote: “Connect your AI with ClickUp using our MCP Server.”
verdicts.reason: The vendor’s developer site and guides publish an official, hosted MCP server with setup docs.

verdicts.quote: “Our Public API is available on all ClickUp Plans.”
verdicts.reason: Self‑serve auth plus published REST docs make it buildable today; note standard constraints (per‑token rate limits and some Enterprise‑only endpoints) but no app review/partner gating that blocks shipping.
